title: Regional data provenance evidence workbench — operator template (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, operator-facing workbench template for assembling auditable evidence bundles that prove regional handling of customer data (region pin + residency enforcement). Intended for SRE/ops and onboarding engineers who package evidence for compliance reviews or customer audits.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus: V1 evidence artifacts (network routing, storage location, KMS key metadata, operator logs, and sample request traces).
- Not a legal brief; use this to collect technical provenance to hand to Legal/Compliance.
- Applies to Hosted + Dedicated + Private (VPC) tenants.
- We assume tenant has a region pin set in tenant profile; if missing see triage below.

Quick triage (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm tenant id and claimed region. (cmd: internal-tenant-get --id <TENANT>)
2) Check tenant pin flag: tenant.pin_region and pin_history. If missing, mark as "no-pin-evidence" and escalate.
3) Run routing snapshot: routing-check --tenant <TENANT> --window 24h -> output routing_snapshot.json
4) Capture recent operator logs containing routing decisions: s3://ops-logs/region-routing/YYYYMMDD/<TENANT>-*.log

Minimum evidence bundle (what we deliver):
- metadata.json (see minimal schema below)
- routing_snapshot.json (last 24h)
- kv:storage-manifest.txt (list of storage clusters/regions, object prefixes)
- kms-keys.csv (key_id, region, creation_date, owner_tag)
- sample-trace.ndjson (3 customer requests, redacted PII)
- operator-changelog.txt (any manual overrides with timestamp + operator id)
- screenshot/console-export.png (tenant region dashboard snapshot)
- chain-of-custody.txt (who produced the bundle and when)

Minimal metadata.json schema (flat key:value pairs — keep simple):
- tenant_id: <string>
- claimed_region: <string>
- collected_at: <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ>
- evidence_version: v1
- collector: <operator name/email>
- data_classes_sampled: embeddings, prompts, logs (comma separated)
- retention_policy_applied: yes|no|n/a
- redaction_applied: yes|no
- notes: short free text

Operator checklist (detailed):
[ ] Create ephemeral workspace: /tmp/region-evidence-<TENANT>-<date>
[ ] Run routing-check (store JSON)
[ ] Export storage manifest (explicit cluster+zone mappings)
[ ] Query KMS inventory for keys with tag tenant=<TENANT>
[ ] Pull 3 request traces that cover different data paths (ingest->runtime->archive)
[ ] Validate that archive buckets are in claimed region(s) (match bucket location header)
[ ] Grab console screenshot + per-route dashboard latency/cost snapshot (for audit context)
[ ] Add operator-changelog with timestamp, actions, and links to any internal PRs/slack threads
[ ] Verify PII redaction rules applied to traces; if not, redact locally and note method
[ ] Package bundle as tar.gz and compute sha256sum
[ ] Upload to secure evidence bucket: evidence-uploads/<TENANT>/<date>/<bundle>.tar.gz

Examples and gotchas (notes to self):
- Storage manifest may show multi-region replication. If replication exists, include replication_policy.txt and call out the replicated regions. We prefer to surface replication for review rather than hide it.
- KMS index sometimes stores keys with cloud provider aliases. Use key_alias_resolve.sh to map provider alias -> canonical key id.
- Edge caches: requests served from CDN/edge may not show origin region. Include edge-config.json and TTL policies to explain short-term cache hits.
- Transient proxies: if tenant uses ephemeral proxies (customer-provided), record handshake evidence + proxy IPs.

Packaging conventions (file names):
- metadata.json
- routing_snapshot.json
- storage_manifest.csv
- kms_keys.csv
- sample_trace_1.ndjson (redacted)
- operator_changelog.txt
- sha256sum.txt
- README.txt (short description of bundle contents)

Communication templates (short):
- To customer (audit ready): "Attached is a technical evidence bundle demonstrating that traffic and persisted artifacts for tenant <TENANT> were processed and stored in <CLAIMED_REGION> during <DATE_RANGE>. We've redacted PII where applicable; let us know if you need deeper artifacts under an NDA."
- Internal escalation (legal request): "Need legal review: evidence bundle for <TENANT> shows replication to <REGION_X>. Recommend contract clause check. Ticket: JIRA-XXXX"

Operator play examples (short scenarios):
1) Pin mis-match (customer claims EU pin, evidence shows us-west-2 storage):
   - Flag severity: HIGH
   - Actions: suspend cross-region replication, notify infra-team, open legal ticket, notify customer with initial findings.
2) Operator override present (manual routing override applied):
   - Attach operator_changelog and Slack thread; tag operator for explanation; if override older than 72h escalate to incident review.

Retention and access control for bundles:
- Evidence bundles live for 90 days in evidence-uploads/<TENANT>/ unless legal holds extend retention.
- Access restricted to eng-private-deployments, security, legal. Use SSO group: evidence-reviewers@redwood.ai

FAQ / short answers:
Q: "How many traces do we need?"
A: Minimum 3 that cover distinct code paths (ingest, inference, archive). More if customer demands.

Q: "Can I include raw prompts?"
A: Only if redacted and with approval; otherwise include metadata but redact content fields.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add automated extractor that runs routing-check + kms dump and emits pre-populated metadata.json (ticket: JIRA-2345).
- Decide canonical storage_manifest format (csv vs json).
- Create a short training slide deck for ops (2–3 slides) with screenshots and example commands.

Appendix: quick commands (internal)
- internal-tenant-get --id <TENANT> --fields pin_region,created_at,owner
- routing-check --tenant <TENANT> --window 24h --format json > routing_snapshot.json
- kms-inventory --filter tenant:<TENANT> --format csv > kms_keys.csv
- storage-manifest-export --tenant <TENANT> > storage_manifest.csv
- trace-export --tenant <TENANT> --sample 3 --redact > sample_traces.ndjson

Contact: Aisha Patel (eng-private-deployments) — aisha@redwood.ai
Notes: this is intentionally operational and slightly terse. Use for audits and customer onboarding evidence; hand off to Compliance for final sign-off.
